bullets.creator: Herman Hesse
bullets.note: ** This is one of the books most frequently recommended by podcast guests. Long ago, [Naval Ravikant](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/0vukl0mnnu9hz234oco/q6f8h7h6gg4l6d/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE1LzA4LzE4L3RoZS1ldm9sdXRpb25hcnktYW5nZWwtbmF2YWwtcmF2aWthbnQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9Y29udmVydGtpdCZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTViZg==) ([@naval](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/0vukl0mnnu9hz234oco/33tphkhd662kdz/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9uYXZhbA==)) highlighted for me the protagonist Siddhartha’s response to “What can you give?” His simple answer is “I can think, I can wait, I can fast.” There’s much more to his response ([search “Kamala” here for a good excerpt](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/0vukl0mnnu9hz234oco/4mcvheh2zzp72k/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE2LzEwLzI1L3Rvb2xzLW9mLXRpdGFucy8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1jb252ZXJ0a2l0JnV0bV9tZWRpdW09Y29udmVydGtpdCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249NWJm)), and I think about it often. Skip the Amazon description, as it gives away too much plot, but consider reading or rereading this short gem. If you’d prefer an even shorter read, try this: [Can We All Be Like Texas?](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/0vukl0mnnu9hz234oco/r4s8hoh5993o5k/aHR0cHM6Ly9yZWFzb25zdG9iZWNoZWVyZnVsLndvcmxkL3RleGFzLXdpbmQtcG93ZXItcmVuZXdhYmxlLWVuZXJneS8=) by David Byrne ([@DBtodomundo](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/0vukl0mnnu9hz234oco/82aqhoh5ee275z/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9kYnRvZG9tdW5kbw==)).

bullets.title: Betty Eisner
bullets.note: This woman is amazing, and this isn’t my first time reading up on her. I’m revisiting because of my re-engagement with a few scientific projects. To give an example of how these connect, Betty appears to be one of the originators of using “dyads” (simultaneous male and female therapists) during hallucinogen administration, a format that is currently being used to great effect in [the treatment of PTSD using MDMA-assisted psychotherapy](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/0vukl0mnnu9hz234oco/93tzhnh2kk6egq/aHR0cHM6Ly9tYXBzLm9yZy8=). Here’s more on her wide-ranging CV, adapted from Wikipedia: Betty was an American psychologist known for pioneering the use of LSD and other psychedelic drugs as adjuncts to psychotherapy. She conducted early research into the use of LSD to treat alcoholism and maintained an active interest in hallucinogens throughout her career. Eisner was a therapist for Bill Wilson, co-founder of Alcoholics Anonymous, when he tried LSD. In addition to using hallucinogens like LSD and mescaline in psychedelic therapy, Eisner also gave stimulants, such as methylphenidate and the inhaled gas mixture carbogen, to her patients. (For those interested in current research into how compounds like psilocybin can be applied to alcoholism, I highly recommend looking at the [work being done at NYU](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/0vukl0mnnu9hz234oco/nrcohvhowwxlnx/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubWVkc2NhcGUuY29tL3ZpZXdhcnRpY2xlLzkxMzQyMg==).)
